Parent #1926 (SC-07) / #1645 (SC-10). Scoped child adding the real TUI fixture to the terminal consistency fault spec.

## Requirements: Alt-screen ownership survives resize and exits cleanly

### Problem

The fault spec covers high-rate numbered output but not a screen that owns the terminal: alternate screen, application modes, and a redraw driven by an authoritative resize. Without it, a defect that leaks alt-screen content into normal scrollback, or that stops delivering resize during a TUI, has no browser-level witness.

### Scope

- Enter the alternate screen from a real shell (`\x1b[?1049h`) and set application cursor, mouse and bracketed-paste modes; print a TUI marker built through `printf '%s'` so the echoed command line never contains the marker itself.
- Assert xterm reports `alternate` and holds the marker.
- Resize the viewport, wait for the browser grid to change, and assert the PTY received the authoritative size: a `WINCH` trap prints `stty size`, which must match the new grid, inside the same alternate buffer.
- Exit with Ctrl+C, leave the alternate screen, and assert xterm returns to `normal` with no alt-screen marker leaked into the normal buffer.
- Run over both Relay and P2P; no runtime behavior change.

### Success Criteria

- [ ] SC-01 Over Relay and P2P, an alt-screen enter shows `alternate` with the TUI marker, and exit returns `normal` without the TUI marker appearing in the normal buffer.
- [ ] SC-02 An authoritative resize during the TUI changes the browser grid and delivers the same `rows cols` to the PTY, with the redraw printed inside the same alternate buffer.
- [ ] SC-03 Exact PR HEAD Quality / E2E / Case Smoke / trusted Acceptance, and exact merge-SHA Quality / E2E / Cases / Orchestrator Pass.
